It's 7:02. Your little sister is floating above the kitchen table. And Dad just walked through the wall.
Morning! Has anyone seen my keys?
Mom makes breakfast. All of it. In one second.
So, what if everyone got superpowers overnight?
Rules. Everyone wakes up with one power. Nobody gets to choose. And nobody knows how long it lasts.
Your sister can fly. Dad walks through walls. Mom is super fast.
And you? You jump. You push the wall. You stare at a spoon for a full minute.
Nothing. You're the only one with no power at all.
At school, it's chaos. Kids fly to class. A backpack walks by on its own. Someone is invisible.
And your teacher can read minds. So nobody can cheat anymore.
Pop quiz tomorrow. Everyone groans. Out loud, and in their heads.
At lunch, a kid sneezes fire. Lunch is cancelled.
At home, it gets weird. Dad walks through the bathroom door. Every time. Without knocking.
I can't! My hand goes right through!
Mom runs to the store and back in four seconds. She forgets the milk. Twice.
Your sister flies to the top of a tree. And then she's too scared to come down.
I don't like it up here!
And here's something real. Some people already have a tiny superpower.
About one in four people are supertasters. Bitter food, like broccoli, tastes much stronger to them.
So if your sister hates broccoli, maybe it's not her fault.
That night, you can't sleep. Everyone has something special. Except you.
Then you hear something. Your sister thinks: no more broccoli. Dad thinks: where are my keys? The dog thinks: food.
You can hear everyone's thoughts. All of them. And they won't stop.
And tomorrow is the pop quiz. Your teacher can read minds. And now, she's about to find out that you can too.
